assertions.subject: Inflammatory bowel disease
assertions.quote: Inflammatory bowel diseases, particularly Crohn's disease, frequently involve the ileum, and the fistulizing subtype can result in inflammatory communication with the bladder, leading to an enterovesical fistula.

assertions.subject: Crohn's disease
assertions.quote: The incidence of enterovesical fistula among patients with Crohn's disease ranges from 2% to 5%.

assertions.subject: Ulcerative colitis
assertions.quote: Although uncommon, ulcerative colitis can result in colovesical and ureteric fistulas, particularly in cases with severe inflammation or complications, eg, perforation, fulminant colitis, and obstruction.

assertions.subject: Malignancy
assertions.quote: Malignancy, including colorectal and small bowel cancers, represents the second most common cause of colovesical and enterovesical fistulas, accounting for approximately 10% to 20% of cases.
